lines.trans: I made a brief appearance on 2 Days & 1 Night as the chief producer.
We filmed for twenty minutes and maybe ten minutes will air, so I was wondering how much the appearance fee is.
What friendship do I have with 2 Days & 1 Night to do an unpaid friendly cameo—we are strictly formal seniors and juniors!
I am not an announcer—strictly speaking, I am closer to an ordinary citizen!
Then at least deposit it into a different account instead of my paycheck account!
Then you got burned at the admin desk too!
Complaints have reached a boiling point lately—we need collective action to fix that attitude!
No need to go that far.

words.gloss: all the way to that extent

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
Did you hear about this 1 night?
I was busy today because of 1 night.
Did you hear about this 2 days?
I was busy today because of 2 days.
Did you hear about this chief, responsible?
I was busy today because of chief, responsible.

meanings.note: loanword from English 'producer', often abbreviated as PD (피디) in Korea

examples.trans: Seung-chan is a rookie producer at a broadcasting station.
Who is the producer of that variety show?

meanings.en: for a moment; briefly; a second
meanings.note: Used to soften requests or indicate a very short duration.

examples.trans: Do you have a moment?
Just a second, I'll be right there.
Did you hear about this appearing on the show?
I was busy today because of appearing on the show.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.
Did you hear about this filming too?
I was busy today because of filming too.

examples.text: 촬영은 20분 했고 방송은 10분 나오려나, 그래서 출연료가 어떻게 되나 하고.
examples.trans: We filmed for twenty minutes and maybe ten minutes will air, so I was wondering how much the appearance fee is.
Here the word for 'twenty minutes' is key.

meanings.note: Refers to both the act of broadcasting and the aired program itself.

examples.trans: That program airs on Sunday evening.
Please turn off your phone during the broadcast.

examples.text: 촬영은 20분 했고 방송은 10분 나오려나, 그래서 출연료가 어떻게 되나 하고.
examples.trans: We filmed for twenty minutes and maybe ten minutes will air, so I was wondering how much the appearance fee is.
Here the word for 'ten minutes' is key.

meanings.en: to appear, be published, be achieved (a score/result)
meanings.note: Used for ratings, test scores, or results coming out

examples.trans: I came outside from the house.
The exam results came out well.
So how is it?
So I went.
Did you hear about this appearance fee?
I was busy today because of appearance fee.
How did you get here?
How should we solve this problem?

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?

examples.text: 내가 1박 2일이랑 무슨 우정이 있다고 우정 출연을 하나, 깍듯한 선후배 사이지!
examples.trans: What friendship do I have with 2 Days & 1 Night to do an unpaid friendly cameo—we are strictly formal seniors and juniors!
Here the word for 'friendship' is key.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)

meanings.note: Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

examples.text: 내가 1박 2일이랑 무슨 우정이 있다고 우정 출연을 하나, 깍듯한 선후배 사이지!
examples.trans: What friendship do I have with 2 Days & 1 Night to do an unpaid friendly cameo—we are strictly formal seniors and juniors!
This expression comes from 'strictly polite'.

examples.text: 내가 1박 2일이랑 무슨 우정이 있다고 우정 출연을 하나, 깍듯한 선후배 사이지!
examples.trans: What friendship do I have with 2 Days & 1 Night to do an unpaid friendly cameo—we are strictly formal seniors and juniors!
Here the word for 'senior-junior' is key.
Did you hear about this relationship?
I was busy today because of relationship.

examples.text: 아나운서는 아니잖아, 굳이 따지자면 일반인에 가깝지!
examples.trans: I am not an announcer—strictly speaking, I am closer to an ordinary citizen!
Here the word for 'as for an announcer' is key.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.
I understand well (going out of your way).
Today is a (going out of your way) busy day.

examples.text: 아나운서는 아니잖아, 굳이 따지자면 일반인에 가깝지!
examples.trans: I am not an announcer—strictly speaking, I am closer to an ordinary citizen!
This expression comes from 'strictly speaking'.

examples.text: 일반인 훈남한테 빠진 톱스타 같은 거네요?
examples.trans: So it's like a top star falling for an ordinary handsome guy?
The topic of ordinary non-celebrity came up during this shoot.
The station is close to my house.
We are very close friends.
Then let's meet tomorrow.
Then we're at the same company!
Did you hear about this instead of?
I was busy today because of instead of.

examples.text: 그럼 대신 계좌는 월급 계좌 말고 딴 걸로 좀!
examples.trans: Then at least deposit it into a different account instead of my paycheck account!
Here the word for 'as for the bank account' is key.
I received my salary.
first paycheck

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.
Do not be late, and come early.

examples.text: 그럼 대신 계좌는 월급 계좌 말고 딴 걸로 좀!
examples.trans: Then at least deposit it into a different account instead of my paycheck account!
Here the word for 'another, different' is key.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Used by a younger male to address an older brother or close older male friend/colleague.

examples.trans: Hey, do you have time tonight?
My older brother is an office worker.

meanings.en: to suffer / be on the receiving end of
meanings.note: Used when someone is the victim or recipient of an undesirable event

examples.trans: My friend got hit in a fender-bender yesterday.
Be careful not to fall victim to voice phishing.

meanings.note: Often used adverbially without a particle or with topic particle -은.

examples.trans: The weather is really nice nowadays.
I'm busy these days so I can't exercise.

examples.text: 요즘 불만이 극에 달해 있어요, 우리가 단체 행동을 해서 버릇을 고쳐놔야 돼!
examples.trans: Complaints have reached a boiling point lately—we need collective action to fix that attitude!

examples.text: 요즘 불만이 극에 달해 있어요, 우리가 단체 행동을 해서 버릇을 고쳐놔야 돼!

meanings.note: Interrogative or indefinite pronoun; often shortened to 뭐 in casual speech.

examples.trans: What is your favorite food?
What can I help you with?
See you again!
It is raining again.
Please don't say it like that.
It's not that difficult compared to what I thought.

meanings.note: reflexive pronoun referring back to the subject

examples.trans: You have to look after your own rice bowl.
Do your own work yourself.

examples.text: 자기가 뭔데 이면지를 써라 말라 유세합니까, 종이가 자기 겁니까?
examples.trans: Who is she to boss us around about scrap paper—does the station paper belong to her?
Here the word for 'scrap paper' is key.

meanings.note: Irregular ㅡ-stem verb: 쓰다 + -어 becomes 써.
Commonly used for tools, money, or time.

examples.trans: I write in my diary every night.
I wrote my name on the very first page of the book.

examples.text: 자기가 뭔데 이면지를 써라 말라 유세합니까, 종이가 자기 겁니까?
examples.trans: Who is she to boss us around about scrap paper—does the station paper belong to her?
This expression comes from 'throws her weight around'.

examples.text: 너네 팀이 종이 타러 가면 행정반에서 별소리 안 하고 주지?
examples.trans: When your team goes to pick up paper, the admin desk hands it over without a fuss, right?
Here the word for 'paper' is key.
This is my friend Minsu.
He/she did it all.

meanings.note: Contraction of 이 아이; used when introducing or referring to someone younger or close

examples.text: 얜 또 뭐래니, 시간 너무 많네!
examples.trans: What is he going on about now—somebody has way too much free time!
This expression comes from 'what is he babbling about'.

meanings.note: Used with native Korean numbers to count hours (한 시간 = one hour).

examples.trans: Do you have time?
It takes two hours.

meanings.note: Used colloquially for positive or negative emphasis.
Original sense of exceeding a limit.

examples.trans: The weather is so nice today.
Don't worry too much.

meanings.en: to be many, numerous, or abundant
meanings.note: Used for both countable and uncountable nouns.

examples.trans: Because it's the weekend, there are many people at the department store.

examples.text: 오늘 해야 할 일이 너무 많다.
examples.trans: There is too much work to do today.
Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.
